newsitem.title: UK: Oversold gold could bounce to $375 -- UBS.
newsitem.headline: Oversold gold could bounce to $375 -- UBS.

text.p: Gold prices can expect to meet "significant upside resistance" between $374.50 and $378.00 per ounce when the market begins to rally, according to technical analyst Amanda Sells in Union Bank of Switzerland's (UBS) Precious Metals Outlook released on Monday.
The resistance from the former support band will be exacerbated by the intermediate downtrend, adverse momentum and bearish major averages, Sells said.
However gold's fall has made it oversold making possible a near term bounce with a 50-percent retracement target at $375.00.
But she warned that although gold's fall this quarter to $366 "may repreent a final shake-out of adverse sentiment, there is little to support an imminent long term reversal".
"The risk remains therefore with depressed trading within the prevailing downtrend. The worst case scenario is a pattern target of $345 via significant support at $350," Sells said.
Silver's technical profile suggested a fall within its current 12-month downtrend to $4.40.
"Failure here would provoke a further significant decline perhaps to $4.10," she said.
Downside pressure is reinforced by the major moving averages falling but momentum at the shorter end may encourage sideways consolidation near term.
Key resistance for silver occurred at $5.00 and $5.25.
Platinum also has near-term bounce potential after its recent accelerated fall took it into oversold teritory, Sells said.
"In the absence of any new negative divergence...a 50 percent retracement to $379.00 is feasible," she said.
At that level it will run into "restrictive physical and downtrend pressure" and for the techncial picture to become more positive a clear break of $390.00 would be needed.

"Such a reversal is not supported by the current technical profile. The risk remains of further downside weakness within the prevailing downtrend," Sells said, adding that significant support levels are at $350.00 and $330.00.
